title: Long-Term Impact of the BNT162b2 mRNA Vaccine on Graft Function in Lung Transplant Recipients: A Single-Center Retrospective Study
content: Background: BNT162b2 vaccination is considered safe in the general population and in solid organ transplant recipients. However, concerns persist that it may induce donor-specific antibodies (DSAs) and trigger rejection in lung transplant recipients (LTRs), and long-term data are limited. This study evaluates the impact of BNT162b2 vaccination on graft function in LTRs. Methods: We retrospectively analyzed 139 LTRs from a prospective cohort study conducted between December 2020 and December 2023. Variables included demographics, acute cellular rejection (ACR), de-novo DSA development, and chronic lung allograft dysfunction (CLAD). Results: Three BNT162b2 doses did not significantly increase rejection risk. ACR occurred in 2.8% of patients, consistent with pre-vaccination rates, and no de-novo DSAs were detected after two doses. Lung function remained stable in all patients at six months. Over 36 months, 87% of LTRs maintained stable FEV1, while 18 patients experienced graft function decline, including 11 (7%) who developed CLAD. Pre-vaccination CLAD and six-month post-vaccination FEV1 were independent risk factors for graft deterioration (HR 4.950, 95% CI 1.560–15.709, p=0.007; HR 1.065, 95% CI 1.018–1.115, p=0.006, respectively), whereas elevated post-vaccination antibody titers and ACR were not predictive. Thirty-six-month survival was 89%, with older age and pre-existing CLAD identified as risk factors for mortality. Conclusions: BNT162b2 vaccination poses minimal risk to graft function in LTRs, supporting its continued use for protecting this population against COVID-19.
